claim: Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived neurons are increasingly used to model Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD).
source: Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived neurons are increasingly used to model Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), which is clinically and genetically heterogeneous.
evidence: This is a statement about current research practice in the field, supported by the context of the manuscript and general scientific knowledge.

claim: ASD is clinically and genetically heterogeneous.
source: Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived neurons are increasingly used to model Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), which is clinically and genetically heterogeneous.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction section referencing established literature on ASD heterogeneity.

claim: 53 different iPSC-derived glutamatergic neuronal lines were generated from 25 participants from 12 unrelated families with ASD.
source: We developed a set of procedures to control for heterogeneity in reprogramming and differentiation, and generated 53 different iPSC-derived glutamatergic neuronal lines from 25 participants from 12 unrelated families with ASD.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental work performed, supported by the data presented in Table 1 and throughout the manuscript.

claim: Heterozygous de novo and rare-inherited presumed-damaging variants were characterized in ASD risk genes/loci.
source: Heterozygous de novo and rare-inherited presumed-damaging variants were characterized in ASD risk genes/loci.
evidence: This is supported by the genetic characterization data presented in Table 1 and Figure 1.

claim: A reproducible synaptic phenotype was determined in 25% of the individuals with ASD.
source: We used a multi-electrode array, with patch-clamp recordings, to determine a reproducible synaptic phenotype in 25% of the individuals with ASD (other relevant data on the remaining lines was collected).
evidence: This is based on the experimental results from MEA and patch-clamp recordings presented in the manuscript.

claim: CNTN5-deficient neurons exhibit consistent spontaneous network hyperactivity.
source: Our most compelling new results revealed a consistent spontaneous network hyperactivity in neurons deficient for CNTN5 or EHMT2.
evidence: This is supported by MEA data shown in Figures 3 and 4, demonstrating increased weighted mean firing rate and network burst frequency.

claim: EHMT2-deficient neurons exhibit consistent spontaneous network hyperactivity.
source: Our most compelling new results revealed a consistent spontaneous network hyperactivity in neurons deficient for CNTN5 or EHMT2.
evidence: This is supported by MEA and patch-clamp data shown in Figures 3 and 6, demonstrating increased neuronal activity.

claim: The past two decades of research has determined autism spectrum disorders (ASD) to be clinically heterogeneous.
source: The past two decades of research has determined autism spectrum disorders (ASD) to be clinically (Fernandez and Scherer, 2017; Jones and Lord, 2013; Mahdi et al., 2018) and genetically (De Rubeis et al., 2014; Gilman et al., 2011; Pinto et al., 2014; Tammimies et al., 2015; C Yuen et al., 2017) heterogeneous.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The past two decades of research has determined autism spectrum disorders (ASD) to be genetically heterogeneous.
source: The past two decades of research has determined autism spectrum disorders (ASD) to be clinically (Fernandez and Scherer, 2017; Jones and Lord, 2013; Mahdi et al., 2018) and genetically (De Rubeis et al., 2014; Gilman et al., 2011; Pinto et al., 2014; Tammimies et al., 2015; C Yuen et al., 2017) heterogeneous.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The fifth edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5) combines autistic disorder, Asperger disorder, childhood disintegrative disorder and pervasive developmental disorder not otherwise specified into the single grouping of ASD.
source: Phenotypically, the fifth edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5) combines autistic disorder, Asperger disorder, childhood disintegrative disorder and pervasive developmental disorder not otherwise specified into the single grouping of ASD (DSM-5, 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about the DSM-5 classification system, supported by citation to the DSM-5.

claim: There are syndromic forms of ASD.
source: There are also syndromic forms of ASD (Carter and Scherer, 2013), and now more than 100 other disorders carrying different names (Betancur, 2011), that in a proportion of subjects can also present the necessary symptoms for an ASD diagnosis.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: More than 100 other disorders can present the necessary symptoms for an ASD diagnosis in a proportion of subjects.
source: There are also syndromic forms of ASD (Carter and Scherer, 2013), and now more than 100 other disorders carrying different names (Betancur, 2011), that in a proportion of subjects can also present the necessary symptoms for an ASD diagnosis.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Heritability estimates and family studies demonstrate genes to be involved in ASD.
source: From the perspective of genetics, heritability estimates and family studies definitely demonstrate genes to be involved (Ronald and Hoekstra, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature on ASD genetics.

claim: Single high-penetrance genes and copy number variation (CNV)-affected loci have been implicated as bona fide autism-susceptibility genes.
source: Single high-penetrance genes and copy number variation (CNV)-affected loci, have now been implicated as bona fide autism-susceptibility (or risk) genes, although none of them show specificity for ASD alone (Malhotra and Sebat, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: None of the identified autism-susceptibility genes show specificity for ASD alone.
source: Single high-penetrance genes and copy number variation (CNV)-affected loci, have now been implicated as bona fide autism-susceptibility (or risk) genes, although none of them show specificity for ASD alone (Malhotra and Sebat, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: ASD genetic alterations are rare in the population (<1% population frequency).
source: These genetic alterations are rare in the population (<1% population frequency), and in some individuals, combinations of rare genetic variants affecting different genes can be involved (Devlin and Scherer, 2012), including more complex structural alterations of chromosomes (Brandler et al., 2018; Marshall et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature on ASD genetics.

claim: In some individuals with ASD, combinations of rare genetic variants affecting different genes can be involved.
source: These genetic alterations are rare in the population (<1% population frequency), and in some individuals, combinations of rare genetic variants affecting different genes can be involved (Devlin and Scherer, 2012), including more complex structural alterations of chromosomes (Brandler et al., 2018; Marshall et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Polygenic contributors may be involved in ASD.
source: Recent research studying common genetic variants indicates that polygenic contributors may be involved, and these can also influence the clinical severity of rare penetrant variants in ASD risk genes (Weiner et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Polygenic contributors can influence the clinical severity of rare penetrant variants in ASD risk genes.
source: Recent research studying common genetic variants indicates that polygenic contributors may be involved, and these can also influence the clinical severity of rare penetrant variants in ASD risk genes (Weiner et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Nearly 1000 putative ASD risk loci are catalogued.
source: Nearly 1000 putative ASD risk loci are catalogued, with ~100 already being used in the clinical diagnostic setting (Hoang et al., 2018a; Winden et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Approximately 100 ASD risk loci are already being used in the clinical diagnostic setting.
source: Nearly 1000 putative ASD risk loci are catalogued, with ~100 already being used in the clinical diagnostic setting (Hoang et al., 2018a; Winden et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Some genotype-phenotype associations are emerging in ASD, including general trends considering medical complications and IQ.
source: There are some genotype-phenotype associations emerging, including general trends considering medical complications and IQ (Bishop et al., 2017; Sanders et al., 2015; Tammimies et al., 2015), sibling variability depending on the ASD gene variant they carry (Yuen et al., 2015), and lower adaptive ability in those carrying variants compared to affected siblings without the same genetic change (C Yuen et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Sibling variability in ASD depends on the ASD gene variant they carry.
source: There are some genotype-phenotype associations emerging, including general trends considering medical complications and IQ (Bishop et al., 2017; Sanders et al., 2015; Tammimies et al., 2015), sibling variability depending on the ASD gene variant they carry (Yuen et al., 2015), and lower adaptive ability in those carrying variants compared to affected siblings without the same genetic change (C Yuen et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Individuals carrying ASD variants have lower adaptive ability compared to affected siblings without the same genetic change.
source: There are some genotype-phenotype associations emerging, including general trends considering medical complications and IQ (Bishop et al., 2017; Sanders et al., 2015; Tammimies et al., 2015), sibling variability depending on the ASD gene variant they carry (Yuen et al., 2015), and lower adaptive ability in those carrying variants compared to affected siblings without the same genetic change (C Yuen et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Many ASD risk genes are connected into gene networks including those involved in synaptic transmission, transcriptional regulation, and RNA processing functions.
source: Many of the ASD risk genes identified are connected into gene networks including those involved in synaptic transmission, transcriptional regulation, and RNA processing functions (Bourgeron, 2015; De Rubeis et al., 2014; Geschwind and State, 2015; Pinto et al., 2014; Sahin and Sur, 2015; C Yuen et al., 2017; Yuen et al., 2016), with the impacted genes being involved in all of prenatal, region-specific, or broader brain development (Uddin et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: ASD risk genes are involved in prenatal, region-specific, or broader brain development.
source: Many of the ASD risk genes identified are connected into gene networks including those involved in synaptic transmission, transcriptional regulation, and RNA processing functions (Bourgeron, 2015; De Rubeis et al., 2014; Geschwind and State, 2015; Pinto et al., 2014; Sahin and Sur, 2015; C Yuen et al., 2017; Yuen et al., 2016), with the impacted genes being involved in all of prenatal, region-specific, or broader brain development (Uddin et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: An increased ratio of excitation and inhibition in key neural systems is a general unifying theme emerging from neurophysiologic studies of ASD.
source: Perhaps, a general unifying theme that is emerging from neurophysiologic studies is an increased ratio of excitation and inhibition in key neural systems that can be perturbed by variants in the ASD risk genes, or by environmental variables affecting the same targets (Canitano and Pallagrosi, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature and represents a synthesis of neurophysiologic findings.

claim: The increased ratio of excitation and inhibition in neural systems can be perturbed by variants in ASD risk genes or by environmental variables.
source: Perhaps, a general unifying theme that is emerging from neurophysiologic studies is an increased ratio of excitation and inhibition in key neural systems that can be perturbed by variants in the ASD risk genes, or by environmental variables affecting the same targets (Canitano and Pallagrosi, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: iPSC technology allows accessible cellular models to be developed for the highly heterogeneous ASD.
source: The advent of the induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technology (Takahashi et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2007), followed by cellular re-programming to forebrain glutamatergic neurons (Habela et al., 2016), allows accessible cellular models to be developed for the highly heterogeneous ASD (Beltrão-Braga and Muotri, 2017; Dolmetsch and Geschwind, 2011; Durak and Tsai, 2014; Karmacharya and Haggarty, 2016; Marchetto et al., 2017; Yoon et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature on iPSC technology and ASD modeling.

claim: iPSC-derived neurons carry the same precise repertoire of rare and common genetic variants as the donor proband.
source: Carrying the same precise repertoire of rare and common genetic variants as the donor proband, iPSC-derived neurons represent the best genetic mimic of proband neurons for functional and mechanistic studies.
evidence: This is based on the fundamental principle of iPSC technology and established scientific knowledge.

claim: iPSC-derived neurons represent the best genetic mimic of proband neurons for functional and mechanistic studies.
source: Carrying the same precise repertoire of rare and common genetic variants as the donor proband, iPSC-derived neurons represent the best genetic mimic of proband neurons for functional and mechanistic studies.
evidence: This is based on logical inference from the properties of iPSC technology.

claim: Induced differentiation of iPSCs can be achieved with high efficiency and consistency using transient ectopic expression of the transcription factor NGN2.
source: Induced differentiation can be achieved with high efficiency and consistency using transient ectopic expression of the transcription factor NGN2 (Ho et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2013), and this has been shown to be useful in diverse phenotyping projects (Deneault et al., 2018; Pak et al., 2015; Yi et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature on NGN2-mediated differentiation.

claim: NGN2-mediated differentiation has been shown to be useful in diverse phenotyping projects.
source: Induced differentiation can be achieved with high efficiency and consistency using transient ectopic expression of the transcription factor NGN2 (Ho et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2013), and this has been shown to be useful in diverse phenotyping projects (Deneault et al., 2018; Pak et al., 2015; Yi et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Four 'isogenic' pairs of iPSC lines with or without mutation were created using CRISPR editing.
source: We also used clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) editing (Jinek et al., 2012; Ran et al., 2013) to create four 'isogenic' pairs of lines with or without mutation, to better assess mutational impacts.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental work performed, supported by the methods and results sections.

claim: Participants were enrolled in the Autism Speaks MSSNG whole-genome sequencing (WGS) project.
source: Participants were enrolled in the Autism Speaks MSSNG whole-genome sequencing (WGS) project (C Yuen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a direct statement about participant enrollment, supported by citation.

claim: All ASD and related control-participants were initially consented for WGS and upon return of genetic results, then consented for the iPSC study.
source: All ASD and related control-participants were initially consented for WGS and upon return of genetic results, then consented for the iPSC study, using approved protocols through the Research Ethics Board at the Hospital for Sick Children (see Materials and methods section for details) (Hoang et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the consent process.

claim: The study took place over a 5 year period.
source: The study took place over a 5 year period and used incrementally developing ASD gene lists from the following papers (Jiang et al., 2013; Marshall et al., 2008; Tammimies et al., 2015; Yuen et al., 2015) (Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study timeline.

claim: 14 ASD-affected and 11 controls participated in the study.
source: In total, 14 ASD-affected and 11 controls participated, of which 21 were males and four were females (Figure 1 and Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about participant demographics, supported by Table 1 and Figure 1.

claim: 21 males and 4 females participated in the study.
source: In total, 14 ASD-affected and 11 controls participated, of which 21 were males and four were females (Figure 1 and Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about participant demographics, supported by Table 1 and Figure 1.

claim: Cells from either skin fibroblasts or CD34+ blood cells were collected for reprogramming into iPSCs.
source: Cells from either skin fibroblasts or CD34 +blood cells were collected for reprogramming into iPSCs (Figure 2A and Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the cell sources used, supported by Figure 2A and Table 1.

claim: Two different viral approaches were used for cell reprogramming: retroviruses and Sendai virus.
source: Two different viral approaches were used for cell reprogramming. For historical reasons, the first three cell lines in Table 1, namely iPSC IDs 19–2, 19-4 and NR3, were reprogrammed using retroviruses expressing OCT4/POU5F1, SOX2, KLF4 and MYC, and a lentiviral vector that encoded the pluripotency reporter EOS-GFP/PuroR (Hotta et al., 2009). Then, we moved to non-integrative Sendai virus for all the other tested lines (Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the reprogramming methods used, supported by Table 1.

claim: Emerging iPSC colonies were selected for activated endogenous human pluripotency markers, differentiation potential into three germ layer cells after embryoid body formation in vitro, and normal karyotype.
source: Emerging iPSC colonies were selected for activated endogenous human pluripotency markers, differentiation potential into three germ layer cells after embryoid body formation in vitro, and normal karyotype (Figure 2B–D and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement about iPSC characterization criteria, supported by Figure 2B-D and Supplementary file 2.

claim: Two separate pluripotent and karyotypically normal iPSC lines were typically selected per participant for neuronal differentiation and phenotyping experiments.
source: Two separate pluripotent and karyotypically normal iPSC lines were typically selected per participant for neuronal differentiation and phenotyping experiments (Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental design, supported by Table 1.

claim: The NGN2 ectopic expression approach produces highly-enriched populations of glutamatergic neurons within a week.
source: We used the NGN2 ectopic expression approach since highly-enriched populations of glutamatergic neurons can be obtained within a week, and they exhibit robust synaptic activity when co-cultured with glial cells (Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature on the NGN2 method.

claim: NGN2-derived neurons exhibit robust synaptic activity when co-cultured with glial cells.
source: We used the NGN2 ectopic expression approach since highly-enriched populations of glutamatergic neurons can be obtained within a week, and they exhibit robust synaptic activity when co-cultured with glial cells (Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The NGN2 strategy offers highly uniform differentiation levels between cell lines derived from different participants.
source: Importantly, we determined that this strategy offers highly uniform differentiation levels between cell lines derived from different participants (Deneault et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Action potential widths of NGN2-derived neurons are around 1-2 milliseconds.
source: We ensured that the duration and amplitude of detected spikes were similar to typical mammalian neurons, that is, action potential widths of around 1–2 milliseconds (ms) and peak amplitudes of approximately 20–150 µV (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement about measured electrophysiological properties, supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Peak amplitudes of action potentials in NGN2-derived neurons are approximately 20-150 µV.
source: We ensured that the duration and amplitude of detected spikes were similar to typical mammalian neurons, that is, action potential widths of around 1–2 milliseconds (ms) and peak amplitudes of approximately 20–150 µV (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement about measured electrophysiological properties, supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: No substantial change in mean firing rate was observed after addition of the GABA receptor inhibitor PTX.
source: No substantial change was observed after addition of the GABA receptor inhibitor PTX (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), indicating that GABAergic neurons are not appreciably present in our cultures.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: GABAergic neurons are not appreciably present in NGN2-derived cultures.
source: No substantial change was observed after addition of the GABA receptor inhibitor PTX (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), indicating that GABAergic neurons are not appreciably present in our cultures.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of response to PTX treatment.

claim: The mean firing rate was significantly reduced in the presence of the AMPA receptor inhibitor CNQX.
source: However, the MFR was significantly reduced in the presence of the AMPA receptor inhibitor CNQX while unchanged in untreated cells, with a comparable profile across each selected line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Most of the NGN2-derived cultures are composed of glutamatergic neurons.
source: However, the MFR was significantly reduced in the presence of the AMPA receptor inhibitor CNQX while unchanged in untreated cells, with a comparable profile across each selected line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B). This further suggests that most of the cultures were composed of glutamatergic neurons, and that our induction protocol was consistent across different cultures.
evidence: This is an inference based on the response to CNQX treatment.

claim: All neuronal activity was abolished after addition of the sodium channel blocker TTX.
source: All activity was abolished after addition of the sodium channel blocker TTX (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), indicating that our human neurons were expressing functional sodium channels.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: NGN2-derived human neurons express functional sodium channels.
source: All activity was abolished after addition of the sodium channel blocker TTX (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), indicating that our human neurons were expressing functional sodium channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the response to TTX treatment.

claim: The highest weighted mean firing rate for pooled control lines (~1.8 Hz) was detected at week 6.
source: Since the highest wMFR value for this pool of 'all controls' (~1.8 Hz) was detected at week 6 (Figure 3A), we initially used that timepoint to compare the activity of ASD variant and control lines for each family.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 3A.

claim: A significantly higher weighted mean firing rate was recorded in CNTN5-deficient neurons at week 6 compared with their corresponding familial control neurons.
source: In two different families, that is, CNTN5 and EHMT2, a significant higher wMFR was recorded in ASD variant neurons at week 6 compared with their corresponding familial control neurons (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 3B.

claim: A significantly higher weighted mean firing rate was recorded in EHMT2-deficient neurons at week 6 compared with their corresponding familial control neurons.
source: In two different families, that is, CNTN5 and EHMT2, a significant higher wMFR was recorded in ASD variant neurons at week 6 compared with their corresponding familial control neurons (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 3B.

claim: EHMT2-deficient neurons had a strikingly increased weighted mean firing rate at all timepoints from week 4 to 8.
source: EHMT2 had a strikingly increased wMFR at all timepoints, whereas CNTN5 at other timepoints was equivalent to its controls.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 3B.

claim: CNTN5-deficient neurons at timepoints other than week 6 were equivalent to controls.
source: EHMT2 had a strikingly increased wMFR at all timepoints, whereas CNTN5 at other timepoints was equivalent to its controls.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 3B.

claim: No significant differences in weighted mean firing rate were observed for DLGAP2, CAPRIN1, SET or GLI3 variants.
source: In contrast, no significant differences were observed for DLGAP2, CAPRIN1, SET or GLI3 (Figure 3C), suggesting that these variants do not differ from control neuronal activity in our MEA assays, and therefore were not studied further.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 3C.

claim: Different dynamics of altered weighted mean firing rate were observed for ANOS1 and VIP at week 4.
source: Different dynamics of altered wMFR were observed for ANOS1 and VIP at week 4 (Figure 3D), and the ANOS1 nonsense variant was ranked as an example of a candidate for further study.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 3D.

claim: A significantly lower weighted mean firing rate was recorded at weeks 7 and 8 for THRA-mutant neurons.
source: Conversely, a significant lower wMFR was recorded at weeks 7 and 8 for THRA (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 3D.

claim: A significantly lower weighted mean firing rate was observed at weeks 5 and 7 for AGBL4-mutant neurons compared to pooled controls.
source: When we compared their values to the pooled values recorded from all the different familial controls available, no difference was found for NRXN1 and a significantly lower wMFR was observed at weeks 5 and 7 for AGBL4 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 3E.

claim: Most lines from an individual were not significantly different from each other.
source: Most lines from an individual were not significantly different from each other, and reassuringly low inter-individual variability was observed with different siblings bearing the same mutation(s), for example 48K and 48N versus 49G and 49H (SET), or 61I and 61K versus 62M and 62X (GLI3), at different timepoints (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 3F.

claim: Low inter-individual variability was observed with different siblings bearing the same mutation(s).
source: Most lines from an individual were not significantly different from each other, and reassuringly low inter-individual variability was observed with different siblings bearing the same mutation(s), for example 48K and 48N versus 49G and 49H (SET), or 61I and 61K versus 62M and 62X (GLI3), at different timepoints (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 3F.

claim: A significantly higher network burst frequency was observed in CNTN5-mutant neurons at weeks 5, 6 and 8.
source: To further characterize the heterozygous CNTN5-mutant neuron lines 27H and 27N, we first showed a significantly higher network burst frequency at weeks 5, 6 and 8 (Figure 4A), indicating a more synchronized neuronal activity across each well.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 4A.

claim: CNTN5-mutant neurons show more synchronized neuronal activity across each well.
source: To further characterize the heterozygous CNTN5-mutant neuron lines 27H and 27N, we first showed a significantly higher network burst frequency at weeks 5, 6 and 8 (Figure 4A), indicating a more synchronized neuronal activity across each well.
evidence: This is an inference based on the increased network burst frequency.

claim: CNTN5 protein levels overall were reduced by at least 33% in CNTN5-/+ neurons.
source: Importantly, CNTN5 protein levels overall were reduced by at least 33% in CNTN5-/+ neurons (Figure 4A, right panel), suggesting that the 676 kb heterozygous loss in CNTN5 interferes with the production of CNTN5 protein, but also that the non-deleted allele may be more active transcriptionally than in controls.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by the western blot in Figure 4A.

claim: The 676 kb heterozygous loss in CNTN5 interferes with the production of CNTN5 protein.
source: Importantly, CNTN5 protein levels overall were reduced by at least 33% in CNTN5-/+ neurons (Figure 4A, right panel), suggesting that the 676 kb heterozygous loss in CNTN5 interferes with the production of CNTN5 protein, but also that the non-deleted allele may be more active transcriptionally than in controls.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reduced protein levels in heterozygous mutant neurons.

claim: The non-deleted CNTN5 allele may be more active transcriptionally than in controls.
source: Importantly, CNTN5 protein levels overall were reduced by at least 33% in CNTN5-/+ neurons (Figure 4A, right panel), suggesting that the 676 kb heterozygous loss in CNTN5 interferes with the production of CNTN5 protein, but also that the non-deleted allele may be more active transcriptionally than in controls.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that protein levels are reduced by only 33% rather than 50%.

claim: The isogenic iPSC-derived neuron line 19-2-CNTN5StopTag/+ did not show significant differences in weighted mean firing rate or network burst frequency at week 6.
source: Intriguingly, the new isogenic iPSC-derived neuron line 19–2-CNTN5StopTag/+ did not show significant differences in terms of wMFR or network burst frequency at week 6 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 4B.

claim: The weighted mean firing rate of line 19-2 increased up to nearly 3 Hz at week 8.
source: However, the wMFR of line 19–2 increased up to nearly 3 Hz at week 8 (Figure 4B) while the CNTN5 family controls stayed around 0.5 Hz (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 4B.

claim: The hyperactive weighted mean firing rate of 19-2-CNTN5StopTag/+ was only evident from week 10.
source: In this context of a more active cell line, we extended the recordings until week 11, and the hyperactive wMFR of 19–2-CNTN5StopTag/+ was only evident from week 10 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 4B.

claim: CNTN5 protein levels were clearly decreased in the isogenic mutant line 19-2-CNTN5StopTag/+.
source: Moreover, CNTN5 protein levels were clearly decreased in this isogenic mutant line (Figure 4B, right panel), implying that StopTag insertion efficiently disrupted gene expression.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by the western blot in Figure 4B.

claim: StopTag insertion efficiently disrupted CNTN5 gene expression.
source: Moreover, CNTN5 protein levels were clearly decreased in this isogenic mutant line (Figure 4B, right panel), implying that StopTag insertion efficiently disrupted gene expression.
evidence: This is an inference based on the decreased protein levels in the StopTag mutant line.

claim: Loss of CNTN5 function is responsible for increased neuronal activity in vitro.
source: These results indicate that loss of CNTN5 function is responsible for increased neuronal activity in vitro.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results from both the familial and isogenic CNTN5-deficient lines.

claim: After detecting 7% edited cells using droplet digital PCR in well G08, two subsequent limiting-dilution enrichment steps were necessary to isolate a 100% corrected iPSC line.
source: Indeed, after detecting 7% edited cells using droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) in well G08 in the primary 96-well culture plate post-nucleofection, two subsequent limiting-dilution enrichment steps were necessary to isolate a 100% corrected iPSC line (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental procedure and results, supported by Figure 5B.

claim: Sanger sequencing confirmed the properly corrected genomic DNA sequence in line 18CW.
source: Sanger sequencing confirmed the properly corrected genomic DNA sequence (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 5C.

claim: The CRISPR-corrected line 18CW exhibited a significant difference in weighted mean firing rate compared with its isogenic counterpart 18C at 4 weeks.
source: The CRISPR-corrected line 18CW exhibited a significant difference in wMFR compared with its isogenic counterpart 18C at 4 week, and no difference from the familial control line 19A (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 3D.

claim: Significantly lower outward membrane current at 40 mV was detected in the ANOS1-mutant line 18C compared to its isogenic control 18CW.
source: Using this protocol, we detected significantly lower outward membrane current at 40 mV in the mutant line 18C compared to its isogenic control 18CW (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 5D.

claim: A significantly higher inward current was observed in ANOS1-mutant neurons between -40 and 0 mV.
source: A significantly higher inward current was also observed in mutant neurons between −40 and 0 mV (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 5D.

claim: ANOS1-null iPSC-derived glutamatergic neurons present abnormal sodium and potassium membrane currents that might contribute to ASD development.
source: These results indicate that ANOS1-null iPSC-derived glutamatergic neurons present abnormal sodium and potassium membrane currents that might contribute to ASD development.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the patch-clamp results, with speculation about contribution to ASD.

claim: Lines 38B and 38E from participant 6-0393-003 carry a de novo missense E78K in UBE2I and a de novo frameshift variant K1164Nfs in EHMT2.
source: Lines 38B and 38E from participant 6-0393-003 carry two ASD-relevant variants; a de novo missense E78K in UBE2I and a de novo frameshift variant K1164Nfs in EHMT2 (Figure 1L and Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the genetic variants in these lines, supported by Figure 1L and Table 1.

claim: MEA recordings showed a significantly higher weighted mean firing rate in lines 38B/38E from week 4 to 8 compared to their related control line 37E.
source: MEA recordings showed a significantly higher wMFR (Figure 3B) and network burst frequency (Figure 6A) from week 4 to 8 PNI compared to their related control line 37E.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figures 3B and 6A.

claim: MEA recordings showed a significantly higher network burst frequency in lines 38B/38E from week 4 to 8 compared to their related control line 37E.
source: MEA recordings showed a significantly higher wMFR (Figure 3B) and network burst frequency (Figure 6A) from week 4 to 8 PNI compared to their related control line 37E.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figures 3B and 6A.

claim: Intrinsic properties (capacitance and resistance) did not vary significantly between lines 37E and 38E.
source: Intrinsic properties, for example capacitance and resistance, did not vary significantly (Figure 6B), indicating comparable maturity levels between lines 37E and 38E.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 6B.

claim: Lines 37E and 38E have comparable maturity levels.
source: Intrinsic properties, for example capacitance and resistance, did not vary significantly (Figure 6B), indicating comparable maturity levels between lines 37E and 38E.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similar intrinsic properties.

claim: While spontaneous excitatory post-synaptic current amplitude was unchanged, sEPSC frequency was significantly higher in EHMT2/UBE2I mutant neurons compared to controls.
source: While spontaneous excitatory post-synaptic current (sEPSC) amplitude was unchanged, sEPSC frequency was significantly higher in mutant neurons compared to controls (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 6B.

claim: A potential loss-of-function of UBE2I and/or EHMT2 is involved in ASD-related neuronal dysfunction.
source: These observations suggest that a potential loss-of-function of UBE2I and/or EHMT2 is involved in ASD-related neuronal dysfunction.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed neuronal phenotypes in cells carrying variants in these genes.

claim: ANOS1 is a glycoprotein of the extracellular matrix including four consecutive fibronectin type III domains.
source: ANOS1 (Anosmin 1) is a glycoprotein of the extracellular matrix including four consecutive fibronectin type III domains.
evidence: This is a statement about the protein structure based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Loss-of-function variants in ANOS1 cause Kallmann syndrome.
source: Loss-of-function variants in ANOS1 were shown to cause the Kallmann syndrome, which is characterized by congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism associated with anosmia, delayed puberty and infertility (Dodé and Hardelin, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Kallmann syndrome is characterized by congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism associated with anosmia, delayed puberty and infertility.
source: Loss-of-function variants in ANOS1 were shown to cause the Kallmann syndrome, which is characterized by congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism associated with anosmia, delayed puberty and infertility (Dodé and Hardelin, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Defects in the migration of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons were observed during embryonic development in ANOS1-deficient individuals.
source: Defects in the migration of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons were observed during embryonic development, as well as morphological changes in the basal forebrain cortex (Manara et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: A proband carrying the nonsense variant R423X in ANOS1 and presenting clinical hypogonadotropic hypogonadism was also diagnosed with ASD.
source: In human, a proband carrying the nonsense variant R423X in ANOS1, and presenting clinical hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, was also diagnosed with ASD (Jiang et al., 2013), suggesting a link between ANOS1 and ASD.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: There is a link between ANOS1 and ASD.
source: In human, a proband carrying the nonsense variant R423X in ANOS1, and presenting clinical hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, was also diagnosed with ASD (Jiang et al., 2013), suggesting a link between ANOS1 and ASD.
evidence: This is speculation based on the case report cited.

claim: Glutamatergic neuron activity is influenced by ANOS1.
source: These results indicate that glutamatergic neuron activity is also influenced by ANOS1, which represents a risk gene for ASD.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the patch-clamp results showing membrane current defects in ANOS1-mutant neurons.

claim: ANOS1 represents a risk gene for ASD.
source: These results indicate that glutamatergic neuron activity is also influenced by ANOS1, which represents a risk gene for ASD.
evidence: This is based on the genetic and phenotypic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CNTN5 is an immunoglobulin cell adhesion molecule with four fibronectin type III domains.
source: CNTN5 (Contactin 5) is an immunoglobulin cell adhesion molecule, with four fibronectin type III domains, involved in neurite outgrowth and axon connection in cortical neurons, and was associated with ASD (van Daalen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about the protein structure based on established scientific knowledge and citation.

claim: CNTN5 is involved in neurite outgrowth and axon connection in cortical neurons.
source: CNTN5 (Contactin 5) is an immunoglobulin cell adhesion molecule, with four fibronectin type III domains, involved in neurite outgrowth and axon connection in cortical neurons, and was associated with ASD (van Daalen et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: CNTN5 was associated with ASD.
source: CNTN5 (Contactin 5) is an immunoglobulin cell adhesion molecule, with four fibronectin type III domains, involved in neurite outgrowth and axon connection in cortical neurons, and was associated with ASD (van Daalen et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Different CNVs affecting CNTN5 have been associated with ASD and ADHD, with increased occurrence of hyperacusis.
source: Different CNVs affecting CNTN5 have been associated with ASD and ADHD, with increased occurrence of hyperacusis (Lionel et al., 2011; Mercati et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The yeast complementation assay estimated that the de novo missense variant E78K in UBE2I was not responsible for the electrophysiological phenotypes observed in participant 6-0393-003.
source: Using a yeast complementation assay (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), we estimated that the de novo missense variant E78K in UBE3I was not responsible for the electrophysiological phenotypes observed in participant 6-0393-003 (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: EHMT2 (G9a) is a histone methyltransferase (HMTase) that forms a complex with EHMT1 (GLP) to catalyze mono- and dimethylation of lysine nine on histone H3 (H3K9me1/2).
source: EHMT2 (G9a) is a histone methyltransferase (HMTase) that forms a complex with EHMT1 (GLP) to catalyze mono- and dimethylation of lysine nine on histone H3 (H3K9me1/2) (Rice et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: EHMT1 protein sequence is highly similar to EHMT2.
source: Of note, EHMT1 protein sequence is highly similar to EHMT2 (Deimling et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: EHMT1 haploinsufficiency is involved in intellectual disability (ID) and ASD as part of the Kleefstra syndrome.
source: Actually, EHMT1 haploinsufficiency is involved in intellectual disability (ID) and ASD as part of the Kleefstra syndrome (Kleefstra et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: EHMT2 represses pluripotency genes in embryonic stem cells.
source: EHMT2 represses pluripotency genes in embryonic stem cells (Zylicz et al., 2015) and potentially acts as both repressor of neural progenitor genes and activator of neuronal differentiation (Deimling et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: EHMT2 potentially acts as both repressor of neural progenitor genes and activator of neuronal differentiation.
source: EHMT2 represses pluripotency genes in embryonic stem cells (Zylicz et al., 2015) and potentially acts as both repressor of neural progenitor genes and activator of neuronal differentiation (Deimling et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The frameshift K1164Nfs in EHMT2 is located at the beginning of the post-SET domain.
source: However, it is located exactly at the beginning of the post-SET domain, that is at position 1164 of EHMT2.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the location of the variant in the protein structure.

claim: The frameshift K1164Nfs completely disrupts three conserved cysteine residues in the post-SET domain that normally form a zinc-binding site.
source: The resulting change in the downstream protein sequence completely disrupts three conserved cysteine residues in the post-SET domain that normally form a zinc-binding site with a fourth conserved cysteine close to the SET domain (Zhang et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an inference based on the predicted protein sequence change and citation to published literature on protein structure.

claim: Three conserved cysteine residues in the post-SET domain are essential for HMTase activity.
source: Since these three conserved cysteine residues are essential for HMTase activity, as replacement with serine abolished HMTase activity (Zhang et al., 2002), we suspect that this HMTase activity of EHMT2 is defective in our mutant glutamatergic neurons and potentially related to the observed hyperactivity (Figure 6).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The HMTase activity of EHMT2 is suspected to be defective in mutant glutamatergic neurons carrying the K1164Nfs variant.
source: Since these three conserved cysteine residues are essential for HMTase activity, as replacement with serine abolished HMTase activity (Zhang et al., 2002), we suspect that this HMTase activity of EHMT2 is defective in our mutant glutamatergic neurons and potentially related to the observed hyperactivity (Figure 6).
evidence: This is speculation based on the predicted structural disruption and published literature on protein function.

claim: Evaluation of EHMT2 protein abundance revealed a clear decrease in the mutant lines 38B and 38E compared to the control 37E.
source: Interestingly, evaluation of EHMT2 protein abundance revealed a clear decrease in the mutant lines 38B and 38E, as compared to the control 37E (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by the western blot in Figure 6C.

claim: A reduced expression of EHMT2 increases spontaneous spiking activity and sEPSC frequency of glutamatergic neurons.
source: This suggests that a reduced expression of EHMT2 increases spontaneous spiking activity and sEPSC frequency of glutamatergic neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between reduced EHMT2 protein levels and increased neuronal activity.

claim: In the isogenic line 19-2-EHMT2StopTag/+, weighted mean firing rate and network burst frequency were increased compared to control 19-2 around week 10 PNI and beyond.
source: In this new isogenic line, wMFR and network burst frequency were also increased in iPSC-derived 19–2-EHMT2StopTag/+ neurons compared to control 19–2, around week 10 PNI and beyond (Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: EHMT2 protein levels were reduced by half in 19-2-EHMT2StopTag/+ mutant cells.
source: Accordingly, EHMT2 protein levels were reduced by half in mutant cells (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by the western blot in Figure 6E.

claim: Intrinsic properties showed a significant increase in capacitance and decrease in input resistance in EHMT2-mutant cells at day 21-25 PNI.
source: However, intrinsic properties showed a significant increase in capacitance and decrease in input resistance in mutant cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental results, supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The mutant EHMT2 neurons at 3-4 weeks PNI potentially have a faster maturation rate.
source: These observations suggest that the mutant neurons at 3–4 weeks PNI potentially have a faster maturation rate, however, this phenotype is most pronounced in the hyperactivity recorded by MEAs later at 9–11 weeks PNI.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed changes in intrinsic properties.

claim: The inactivation of one allele of EHMT2 significantly increases spontaneous network activity of excitatory neurons.
source: These results support the conclusion that the inactivation of one allele of EHMT2 significantly increases spontaneous network activity of excitatory neurons, with possible effects on the neuronal maturation process.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results from both the familial and isogenic EHMT2-deficient lines.

claim: EHMT2 inactivation has possible effects on the neuronal maturation process.
source: These results support the conclusion that the inactivation of one allele of EHMT2 significantly increases spontaneous network activity of excitatory neurons, with possible effects on the neuronal maturation process.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed changes in intrinsic properties at earlier timepoints.

claim: Inter-individual variation is more important to consider than intra-individual variation in iPSC studies.
source: It was recently proposed that inter-individual variation, that is the number of probands with similar genetic variants, is more important to consider than intra-individual variation, that is the number of iPSC clones derived from the same individual (Hoffman et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The NGN2 system represents an advantage in terms of cellular homogeneity over classic dual-SMAD inhibition protocols.
source: We preferred to use the NGN2 system over classic dual-SMAD inhibition protocols because in our experience it represents an advantage in terms of cellular homogeneity.
evidence: This is based on the authors' experience and comparison of differentiation methods.

claim: The NGN2 system is faster than other neuronal differentiation protocols.
source: It is also faster than other protocols and produces much higher proportion of glutamatergic neurons that can be studied for ASD (Canitano and Pallagrosi, 2017; Habela et al., 2016) or other neurological disorders (Lin et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature and the authors' experience.

claim: The NGN2 system produces much higher proportion of glutamatergic neurons than other protocols.
source: It is also faster than other protocols and produces much higher proportion of glutamatergic neurons that can be studied for ASD (Canitano and Pallagrosi, 2017; Habela et al., 2016) or other neurological disorders (Lin et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Most NGN2-neurons are assumed to be glutamatergic based on the original publication establishing this technique.
source: We assume that most NGN2-neurons are glutamatergic based on the data presented in the original publication establishing this technique (Zhang et al., 2013), and on our previous publication using high-cell density RNAseq assessment (Deneault et al., 2018).
evidence: This is based on citations to published literature.

claim: NGN2 is known to repress GABAergic differentiation at the advantage of glutamatergic differentiation.
source: We measured the glutamatergic/GABAergic nature of our cultured neurons produced using NGN2 ectopic expression, which is known to repress GABAergic differentiation at the advantage of glutamatergic (Roybon et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: MEA phenotypes may not always predict electrophysiological deficits and vice versa.
source: MEA phenotypes may not always predict electrophysiological deficits and vice versa, as evidenced for ASTN2 in our recent publication (Deneault et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Line 19-2 is generally more active than most other familial lines.
source: Line 19–2 is generally more active than most other familial lines, and this may have delayed emergence of the hyperactive phenotype in isogenic cells until week 10.
evidence: This is based on the experimental data showing higher baseline activity in line 19-2.

claim: The higher baseline activity of line 19-2 may have delayed emergence of the hyperactive phenotype in isogenic cells until week 10.
source: Line 19–2 is generally more active than most other familial lines, and this may have delayed emergence of the hyperactive phenotype in isogenic cells until week 10.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that hyperactivity appeared later in the 19-2 isogenic lines.

claim: EHMT2 impacts the synaptic function of glutamatergic neurons through H3K9me1/2 catalyzing ability.
source: Upon our further validation experiment using a CRISPR-derived isogenic system and an unrelated genetic background (Figure 6D), we propose that EHMT2 impacts the synaptic function of glutamatergic neurons through H3K9me1/2 catalyzing ability.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental results and known function of EHMT2.

claim: For future studies to capture and characterize the electrophysiological impact of ASD variants on human iPSC-NGN2 neurons, it is most beneficial to include both MEA and patch-clamp experiments, across multiple timepoints.
source: Furthermore, our work demonstrates that for future studies to capture and characterize the electrophysiological impact of ASD variants on human iPSC-NGN2 neurons, it is most beneficial to include both MEA and patch-clamp experiments, across multiple timepoints.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the authors' experience and results from the study.

claim: Analyzing multiple mutations and genes at once can lead to the identification of potential endophenotypes.
source: Analyzing multiple mutations and genes at once can lead to the identification of potential endophenotypes, in this case neuronal hyperactivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study design and results.

claim: Neuronal hyperactivity is a potential endophenotype identified in this study.
source: Analyzing multiple mutations and genes at once can lead to the identification of potential endophenotypes, in this case neuronal hyperactivity.
evidence: This is based on the consistent observation of hyperactivity in CNTN5 and EHMT2-deficient neurons.

claim: The hyperactivity phenotype offers the possibility to implement NGN2-based high-throughput drug screening strategies.
source: Such phenotype offers the possibility to implement NGN2-based high-throughput drug screening strategies (Cheng et al., 2017) combining MEA (Tukker et al., 2018) and lines 38B/38E for instance, to discover molecules that may compensate for neuronal hyperactivity.
evidence: This is speculation about future applications based on the identified phenotype.
